posts.title: Plum Village & cynicism
posts.description: This summer I spent a week at Plum Village, a Buddhist monastery in the southwest of France. And this place held up a mirror in a way that I didn't expect. There are lots of ways in which this retreat changed me as a person, but here I want to discuss one specific thing that happened there. Plum Village made me realize that I have grown cynical. posts.title: Compassion is emptiness
posts.description: Violence is complex. It requires systems of thought, rationalizations. Violence requires the redirection of suffering, and the obfuscation of this redirection. Compassion is simple. It thrives on attention. It is always already here. Compassion arises in the empty mind, the present moment. It requires no theories or systems. It grows like weeds left alone. posts.title: Oppressors aren't winners
posts.description: There's this tenacious idea that in an unequal society, those at the top are the winners. That is, if you manage to avoid oppression, and if you manage to do the oppressing yourself, then you've got yourself a good life. I'm a white man in an affluent country, and I'm here to tell you why that's bullshit. Why that's bullshit Men According to some strains of feminism, men are the unambiguous winner
